Suchowola Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Suchowola, Poland

Not demolished. Jews began settling in Suchowola toward the beginning of the 17th century; by 1921, 1,262 (51.3%) were mostly murdered between 1942-1943. This cemetery's exact founding is unknown, though on-site commemoration dates it to the 17th century; before 1939, it was stone-walled with a wooden mortuary. Germans used some matzevot to pave roads during WWII; postwar, the fence was torn down and nearly all tombstones removed. Authorities formally closed the cemetery on January 29, 1963. A 2011 memorial plaque was installed, alongside a separate nearby monument commemorating five named Poles killed by Bolshevik forces on August 9, 1920 - a reminder that the site's history extends beyond its Jewish burials alone.
